newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait MP vows to fight corruption after attack.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait MP vows to fight corruption after attack.

text.p: A leading Kuwaiti opposition parliamentarian who survived an assassination attempt said on Saturday the attack had only strengthened his resolve to fight corruption.

"The attack will not prevent me from continuing to confront cases of corruption and to defend the interests of the Kuwaiti people," he said in a letter to parliament speaker Ahmad al-Saadoun carried by the official news agency KUNA.

"If what happened to me was the tax I had to pay for confronting corruption and those tampering with the people's money, then these evil bullets will only provide me with strength and resolve to safeguard the interests of those...who elected us to represent them," Naibari added.

The attempt provided parliament with momentum and public support to combat alleged corruption and to reiterate demands for clear government action against what some MPs call "public funds thieves," analysts have said.
His brother said earlier that Naibari, whose wife was also hurt in the assault, would fly to the United States on Sunday for further medical care.

His condition allowed him to make the trip nine days after he was hit in the jaw and left shoulder when gunmen opened fire on his car with assault rifles, his younger brother Abdul-Rahman al-Naibari said.
"We will fly to Boston on Sunday aboard a private Emiri aircraft," he said. "Abdullah is talking well but he is unable to move his left arm as easily as before."
Three Kuwaitis and two Iranians have been arrested in connection with the attempt to assassinate Oxford-educated Naibari, a 61-year-old liberal critic of the government.
